content.text: Scottie Scheffler has become one of the best golfers in the world over the last decade, and is now a four-time major champion. Scheffler graduated from the University of Texas with a degree in Finance, having helped the team win three consecutive Big 12 Championships. His first season as a professional saw him be named Korn Ferry Tour Player of the Year and Rookie of the Year as he made the move up to the PGA Tour. He had to wait until 2022 before he secured a major win, but he went on to win four times in the next eight weeks. Victories at the Waste Management Phoenix Open and Arnold Palmer Invitational came close together for Scheffler, who then won the WGC-Dell Technologies Match Play. The incredible run culminated in him becoming a major champion. He won the Masters Tournament at Augusta National, becoming World No.1 in the process. 2023 was a quieter year, but he did claim the Players Championship at TPC Sawgrass. Scheffler would go even better through the spring of 2024, winning four times in five starts. He was victorious at the Arnold Palmer Invitational again, along with retaining his Players Championship crown. Scheffler then won the Masters Tournament for a second time, before winning the RBC Heritage in a Monday finish just eight days later. He added a fifth win before the halfway point of the year, with victory at the Memorial Tournament. That turned into six with his first victory at the Travelers Championship, meaning he won four of the season’s eight Signature Events. Scheffler would finally secure the Tour Championship crown at the end of the 2024 PGA Tour season. He won the FedEx Cup along with, and it would be his eighth win of the year. Just a few weeks earlier, the American had won the Olympic Games Gold Medal at Le Golf National in Paris. He rounded out 2024 with his ninth victory of the calendar year, taking a six-shot victory at the Hero World Challenge. Scheffler then went on to claim his third major title with a victory at the PGA Championship at Quail Hollow in 2025. That was one of three wins in the first half of the season, as he also defended his crown at Jack’s Place. He would then go on to claim the Open Championship crown in the same year, winning at Royal Portrush to take him to within one major of the Grand Slam. He made his Ryder Cup debut in 2021, winning 2.5 points from his three matches, including a resounding 4&3 win over Jon Rahm on Singles Sunday. Scheffler made a second Ryder Cup appearance in Rome in 2023. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) about Scottie Scheffler When and where was Scottie Scheffler born? Scottie Scheffler was born in Ridgewood, New Jersey, United States on June 21, 1996. His parents gave him a set of plastic clubs and ball, and Scheffler started swinging the clubs at the age of 3. He received tutelage from Randy Smith at the Royal Oaks Golf Club after the family moved to Dallas, Texas. When did Scottie Scheffler turn professional? After graduating from the University of Texas with a degree in Finance, Scheffler turned professional in 2018, and earned his Web.com (now Korn Ferry) Tour card for the 2019 season. He then moved up the PGA Tour for the 2019-20 season. How many major titles has Scottie Scheffler won? As of July 2025, Scheffler is a four-time major champion. He has donned the Green Jacket on two occasions, after winning the Masters Tournament in both 2022 and 2024, before then winning the PGA Championship and the Open Championship in 2025. They are a part of a glittering career which has seen him win 20 times on the PGA Tour so far. Who is Scottie Scheffler married to? Scheffler is married to Meredith Scudder. The pair had been together for six years before getting married in 2020. Scudder works for Behind Every Door (BED), a nonprofit organization that provides sport, educational and creative programs for the youth in underdeveloped neighborhoods in the Dallas area. The pair welcomed their first child – Bennett – to the world in May 2024. RELATED: Who are Scheffler’s wife and baby? Meet Meredith and Bennett Scottie Scheffler with wife Meredith Scudder after winning the WM Phoenix Open at TPC Scottsdale in 2023 Did you Know? Four Wins In Six Starts to Reach World No.1 Coming into 2022, Scheffler was yet to win on the PGA Tour. Within four months, he had four victories, including a major title, and was the World No.1. He won the Waste Management Phoenix Open to claim his maiden PGA Tour victory, before then winning the Arnold Palmer Invitational and the WGC-Dell Technologies Match Play. His incredible run was completed with a maiden major crown, winning the Masters Tournament at Augusta National. A Season for the Ages Scheffler’s 2024 campaign was one for the history books. He became the first person to win seven times in a PGA Tour season since Tiger Woods did so in 2007. He also finished the campaign with a scoring average of 68, breaking the record for the lowest scoring average in PGA Tour history. PGA Tour Record Low At the CJ CUP Byron Nelson, Scheffler tied the record for the lowest score (total strokes) in PGA Tour history. He finished with a cumulative total of 253 to join Justin Thomas and Ludvig Aberg in doing so. However, Scheffler’s came on a par 71 course, compared to the par 70s, that Thomas and Aberg recorded a 253 total score. 59 Club Scheffler is part of a small club. He is one of just a handful of golfers to have shoot a 59 on the PGA Tour. That came at the Northern Trust during his rookie campaign. Players Championship History Scheffler fired in a final round of 64 to win The Players Championship in 2024. His victory saw him become the first ever back-to-back winner of the PGA Tour’s flagship event in its 50-year history. Walker Cup Winner with Future Stars The 2017 Walker Cup featured several soon-to-be PGA Tour stars, including Scheffler. Cameron Champ, Doug Ghim, Collin Morikawa and Will Zalatoris were also in the American side that won the competition 19-7 at Los Angeles Country Club.
